newsitem.title: USA: MedCath to open 20 heart hospitals.
newsitem.headline: MedCath to open 20 heart hospitals.

text.p: MedCath Inc Chairman Stephen Puckett said Wednesday the company plans to open its "heart hospitals" in 20 states in the near future.
MedCath provides cardiology and cardiovascular services through the development, operation and management of cardiac-care hospitals.
Federal law had limited the market for such services, but regulators in 20 states have now dropped the so-called "certificate of need" in order to allow competition.
"We're targeting all 20 states," Puckett said during MedCath's annual meeting here.
The company, which also provides specialized cardiac-care facilities as well as manages the practices of 76 physicians, opened its first heart hospital in McAllen, Texas, last year.
Last week it opened another in Little Rock, Ark., and it plans others in Tucson, Ariz., in October, Austin, Texas, in spring of 1998, and Bakersfiled, Calif., in autumn of 1998.
Puckett said he expects competition to increase as more states deregulate.
"The states that have dropped their (certificate of need) are mostly in the West," he said, but Indiana, Ohio and Pennsylvania have also taken the step.
MedCath also has a Diagnostics unit that supplements hospital services via mobile laboratories.

In late morning trading on NASDAQ the company's stock was up 1/2 at 15-1/2. It has hovered around that level since June, when the stock fell more than 50 percent after news reports that the company was recording revenue for Medicare reimbursements for which it had not yet filed.
